scope.invariant: Named state.set derives authority solely from native task identity, rechecks context/epoch/grants/object and namespace versions, commits value/provenance/receipt atomically against revocation, and closes transient authority before acknowledging cancellation. Production IPC exposes named controls and bounded relays without arbitrary authority writers.

declaredStatus.claim: Named operations recheck native authority/version/idempotency and commit data/provenance/receipts with revocation; cancellation closes contexts before its ACK; no production fixture/raw grant/session/general data-relay writers exist.
declaredStatus.assessment: Commit/revoke and bounded IPC checks pass; command cancellation incorrectly acknowledges native close failures.

checks.question: Are named business writes owned by runtime and native persistence instead of renderer apply callbacks?
checks.detail: Broker maps bounded DTOs to a native WriteRequest using task.caller/task.context, then calls prepare/commit. The runtime owns the installation namespace, provenance and receipt; the renderer receives an already committed result.

checks.question: Does cancellation wait for durable session/context closure before reporting success?
checks.detail: A native SQLite session-close write failure is swallowed. Both false-success acknowledgement and a subsequently persisted already-admitted write are reproduced. Successful cancellation control closes authority and rejects the late write.

checks.question: Do commit/revoke, optimistic versions, replay receipts and provenance remain atomic under competition?
checks.detail: Clock/identity/epoch/grants/selected version and namespace expectedVersion are checked within transactions; checked version increments preserve bounds. Identical retries share a receipt; changed operation payloads reject. Two real SQLite connections admit only one conflicting version, and simultaneous commit/revoke produces only the two serially valid outcomes. Revoke-first denies old reservations; commit-first retains value/private provenance/receipt.

checks.question: Are caller identities native and production permissions restricted to named operations?
checks.detail: Native task creation supplies channel/document/account/context and package proof. Relay checks actual WebView/window/document, task lifetime, sequence, request/context and Schema. Static registry checks cover 61 commands and 18 reviewed plugin command names; no raw seed/grant/session/data relay or direct state.set/get command is registered. Main product grants target only main. Native ACL tests resolve all registered commands for executor labels and allow only their relay.
checks.limit: This establishes registry/ACL and the selected call chain, not a complete consent/DEV/package/admission or live relay security audit. B14-R01 remains open on guard time sampling.

checks.detail: 24 runtime tests, 2 executor resource/ACL tests and 1 product-caller test pass. findings.title: Propagate native session-close errors before acknowledging command cancellation
findings.trigger: A running task is canceled while the SQLite transaction that closes its native session fails before COMMIT. A previously admitted relay reaches its blocking broker after the cancel response and storage becomes writable again.
findings.observed: cancel_install discards authority.with(host_end_session) errors and returns unit. plugin_command_cancel consequently returns Ok(()). The failed transaction retains the session/context; after the injected SQLite failure is cleared, the unchanged state.set arm returns version 1 and the late value is persisted.
findings.effect: The user receives a successful cancellation acknowledgement while old native write authority remains usable by already admitted work. This violates the documented close-before-ACK contract. Normal cancellation closes the session and denies the same late write.
findings.limit: Reproduced with the unchanged extracted cancellation method, product-command body and state.set arm, actual runtime and actual SQLite adapter. Native/view setup is headless and the already admitted relay is simulated; no actual WebView race or exploit was executed. The demonstrated late write is confined to the installation namespace, not canonical host library data.
findings.suggestedAction: Make cancel_install return a Result and propagate poisoned-task-lock/session-close failures. Return success from plugin_command_cancel only after every matching session/context has durably closed. Keep already admitted work unable to commit after successful cancellation; cover failure and successful controls with permanent regressions.

inheritedFindings.detail: Pre-transaction Clock sampling in check_context/check_capability is unchanged; its six failing expiry probes remain valid.

probeEvidence.method: The generator copies cancel_install, the product cancel body and selected state.set broker arm verbatim. Test-owned native authority and product/view adapters replace setup only; Caller/session/package fixtures never enter product code. The unchanged SQLite implementation uses a relocated child-test #[path]. Its real fail_before_commit injection rolls back session closure. A direct call to the copied state.set arm models already-admitted relay work after the false ACK.
